newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO to seize unregistered Bosnian army munitions.
newsitem.headline: NATO to seize unregistered Bosnian army munitions.

text.p: The NATO-led peace force said on Thursday it will have to confiscate tank ammunition donated to the Bosnian army through a U.S. military aid programme because the munitions were not properly registered.

Stabilisation Force (SFOR) troops found 474 tank rounds at a northwestern storage site this week which the Bosnian Federation army had failed to document under terms of the peace agreement, said NATO spokesman Major Tony White.
The 105 mm tank ammunition was delivered to Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation earlier this month as part of the U.S.-sponsored "Train and Equip" programme devised to bolster the federation military.
White said NATO troops in Bosnia strictly enforce peacetime rules which require rival armies to fully document all weapons or ammunition stored at designated depots.
"If it's existing equipment or received through "Train and Equip' it doesn't make any difference," White told Reuters.
"This is not the first time poor book-keeping has resulted in confiscation. They have to be more careful."
NATO-led troops have already destroyed a large number of weapons and ammunition confiscated from Serb, Croat and Moslem armies over the past year.
The tank rounds were found at a storage site in Koracina, 10 km (six miles) northwest of Livno in western Bosnia, in an area under British command, White said.
A Sarajevo spokesman for the U.S. aid programme said 11,000 tank rounds for 45 U.S. tanks were shipped to the federation and placed in storage sites.

The United States, with help from Turkey, Egypt and other Islamic countries, has organised the $400 million programme that is supposed to create a military balance between the federation and forces of Bosnia's Serb republic entity.
